citation.title: Robots are both anthropomorphized and dehumanized when harmed intentionally

reading.source_scope_note: Two randomized 2×2 text-vignette experiments with finalN429 and677, plus a separateN75 description pretest. Human observers rate a fictional robot and its caretaker/creator. Harm is contrasted with active maintenance, and emotional simulation/detection is described rather than demonstrated. Pain is a measured mediator; the data do not establish simultaneous mental processes, robot experience or actual changes in observers’ conduct toward people.

study.sample: Experiment1 recruited452, excluded22 faster than134.25s plus one failed timeout, final429. Experiment2 recruited700, excluded21 faster than246s plus two under18, final677; earlier participants excluded by recruitment setting. Main final total1106, plus separate pretest75. English-fluent versus first-language screening differed; reporting summary says no nationality/ethnicity information, limiting a claim of verified Western-cultural coverage.
study.design: Randomized harm/no-harm × emotional-detection-and-simulation/no-emotional-abilities, each between subjects. George is a fictional complex social robot. Harm is repeated scalpel damage; no-harm is repeated re-oiling/maintenance. Experiment1 actor envies the creator; Experiment2 actor is creator and bored with upkeep, explicitly aware of harmful/beneficial actions. No accidental-harm or neutral-inaction condition.
study.pretest: N75: emotional description raises experience ratings3.25 versus1.48 on1–7; agency contrast nonsignificant. This checks relative attribution, not actual emotions, equivalent agency or proof that most individuals endorsed sentience.
study.measures: Single pain-capacity item;18-item overall mind mean excluding pain and consciousness; five-item agency and13-item experience means. Consciousness is one item in Experiment1, two in Experiment2, reported in supplement. Adapted16-item perceived-prosociality scale rates the human actor, not the actor’s actual behavior toward other people.
study.factor_structure: Experiment1 initially yields three PCA components; authors explicitly force two and use five/13-item split. Experiment2 reports two components with same assignment. Direct-oblimin PCA of selected items and high alpha do not prove a universal two-dimensional architecture. Supplement2c saysN670 versus main677; missingness could explain but not reconstructed.
study.main_results: Harm increases attributed pain in both experiments, small effects: F6.047,p.014,partialeta≈.01 and F14.41,p<.001,partialeta≈.02. Emotional-description main effects larger. Formal harm×emotion interactions on pain are nonsignificant,p.67/.24; supplementary Bayesian comparison does not support an interaction under tested priors. This is not proof of zero interaction in every setting.
study.mediation: PROCESS4,5000bootstrap samples, emotion covariate, untransformed pain. Harm indirect effects on overall mind+.13CI[.01,.25] and+.20CI[.10,.30]; adjusted direct−.18CI[−.34,−.02] and−.21CI[−.33,−.09]; total−.05CI[−.25,.15] and−.01CI[−.17,.15]. Rounded products .30×.42≈.126 and .41×.49≈.201 reconcile totals. Opposing paths do not require a significant total effect and are not themselves an arithmetic error.
study.dimension_results: Experience has positive indirect and negative adjusted direct paths; agency positive indirect but nonsignificant adjusted direct paths. Consciousness supplement has positive pain paths but no significant adjusted harm-direct paths. Do not generalize the overall-mind interpretation to every capacity or claim proof of automatic and reflective processes operating simultaneously.
study.prosociality: Harming actor rated less prosocial than caring actor in both studies. Experiment2 has formal harm×emotion interactionF9.30,p.002, with emotion-description difference in no-harm care condition; Experiment1 interaction null. This is impression formation from morally relevant conduct, not proof of a halo bias or causal cruelty spillover toward humans/animals.
study.public_code: Experiment2 COMPUTE lines139–153 confirm means of18 total, five agency and13 experience items. MEAN permits available-item averaging; without raw missingness it cannot definitively repair all table mean identities. Factor analysis uses listwise missingness. Analysis lines414–453 explicitly test full factorial terms atalpha.05; lines456–459 describe mediation but note syntax not saved. No research code executed.
study.addendum: Public addendum states fast-completion exclusions and diagnostic/transformation choices for Experiment1 were made during collection/before analysis, and included in Experiment2 preregistration. It explicitly discloses this distinction; do not mischaracterize it as hidden.

summary: No new entry. Enrich harm-made mind, mind/agency/experience attribution, anthropomorphism and dyadic completion using two replications, preserving opposing indirect/direct paths and null total effects. Record robot-dehumanization as a qualified interpretive analogy. Correct table arithmetic and verified attribution/model labels, retain unresolved numerical discrepancies, and avoid inferring actual sentience, universal dimensionality or cruelty spillover.

findings.definition: Increased attribution of mental capacities to an entity when it is perceived as harmed or victimized.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add two vignette replications, opposing-path evidence and measurement limits rather than a synonymous record.
findings.evidence_scope: Two preregistered-design vignette studies replicate a small increase in pain attribution for an intentionally harmed fictional robot versus an actively cared-for robot. Positive pain-mediated associations with broader mind ratings coexist with negative adjusted direct paths and nonsignificant overall total effects.
findings.boundary: The replicated pain-attribution pattern is narrower than an unconditional increase in all mental capacities. Mediators were measured; opposing regression paths do not prove simultaneous unconscious humanizing and reflective dehumanizing mechanisms or actual robot suffering.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add two vignette replications, opposing-path evidence and measurement limits rather than a synonymous record.

evidence.quote: statistically signiﬁcant evidence for a total effect

findings.evidence_scope: An18-item mean is used for broader mind perception. Harm has no significant total effect in either study, while pain-mediated and adjusted direct paths have opposite signs. Emotional-description framing raises overall ratings. Consciousness is measured separately in the supplement.
findings.boundary: Do not replace total effects with adjusted direct effects, combine consciousness into the18-item score, infer majority belief from a mean, or treat attribution ratings as verified mentality. Forced component selection is not universal dimensional validation.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add two vignette replications, opposing-path evidence and measurement limits rather than a synonymous record.

evidence.quote: For the perceived experience of the robot

findings.evidence_scope: The13-item experience subscale shows positive indirect harm paths through pain but negative adjusted direct paths. Emotion wording increases experience ratings. Items include emotion communication/understanding as well as feeling capacities after an explicitly forced two-component solution in Experiment1.
findings.boundary: Specific subscale composition, opposite paths and exploratory status matter. No causal psychological process is isolated by the measured mediator, and actual feelings, rights or legal standing are not measured.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add two vignette replications, opposing-path evidence and measurement limits rather than a synonymous record.
findings.evidence_scope: Five-item agency attribution has a small positive pain-mediated harm path, but no significant adjusted harm-direct path in either experiment. Agency and experience do not show identical fitted patterns.
findings.boundary: Significance in experience and nonsignificance in agency is not a tested between-outcome difference. This does not show equivalent agency, agency absence or actual intention in the robot.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add two vignette replications, opposing-path evidence and measurement limits rather than a synonymous record.
findings.evidence_scope: Emotional-detection/simulation descriptions increase human mental-capacity attributions. Authors interpret opposing pain-mediated and adjusted harm paths as humanizing/dehumanizing responses, while acknowledging that their data do not identify why the paths oppose.
findings.boundary: Description effects and observer attributions do not validate actual robot emotions, simultaneous latent processes or manipulative intent. A nonsignificant interaction does not establish emotional design never moderates responses.

findings.definition: Inferring a missing moral agent or feeling recipient to complete an apparently helpful or harmful event as an agent–patient moral relationship.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add two vignette replications, opposing-path evidence and measurement limits rather than a synonymous record.
findings.evidence_scope: The theory links perceived victimization to inferred capacity for pain. Two experiments test a predicted harm-linked attribution pattern, but do not separately manipulate a missing dyadic role or discriminate the process from empathy, wording, demand or related explanations.
findings.boundary: Support for a predicted pattern is not unique verification of dyadic completion. Both actor and recipient are described; automaticity and generalization to AI-as-evaluator behavior remain untested.

findings.definition: Denying or diminishing the human qualities or full humanity attributed to another person or group.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add two vignette replications, opposing-path evidence and measurement limits rather than a synonymous record.

evidence.quote: a coping mechanism to reduce feelings of uncanniness

findings.evidence_scope: Dehumanization, harm justification, dual processing and uncanniness are offered as possible explanations of an adjusted negative mind path. Authors explicitly say current data cannot determine its cause; no separate dehumanization scale or process intervention is used.
findings.boundary: This adds an interpretation boundary only, not an independent measured-dehumanization paper. Lower robot mind attribution is not automatically denial of a human’s humanity, proof of motivated coping or a license to reduce human rights.

methodological_limits: Text descriptions, harm versus active care and changed actor motives do not isolate injury, neutral baseline or intentional versus accidental harm. Authors acknowledge these design constraints.

Measured pain and simultaneous self-report composites do not establish a causal latent mediator, automaticity, reflective coping or two opposing processes in every individual. Group-level paths may not hold within persons.
Two online English-screened samples,unknown nationality/ethnicity and fictional robot descriptions do not warrant universal Western-cultural or actual-interaction generalization.
Forced two-component PCA, item overlap and highalpha do not validate a universal dimensional architecture; consciousness instruments change between experiments.

Formal interaction tests exist: pain nulls differ from significant Experiment2 prosociality interaction. Null is not equivalence, and perceived actor prosociality does not establish behavioral cruelty spillover.
Several printed table/model inconsistencies remain unresolved. Safe arithmetic/source-attribution repairs do not authorize silently rewriting reported raw statistics or claiming fraud.
Preregistration deviations in Experiment1 are explicitly disclosed in the public addendum. Partial code inspection without raw data/output is not full replication.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Adds two text-vignette replications with pain-mediated associations but no significant overall-mind total effect. Different outcome composites/control conditions prevent treating every harm-made-mind study as identical.

This earlier paper proposes automatic/reflective opposition as one explanation,which the later Koban study explores more directly. Neither the earlier regression suppression nor the later fixed-order load/review manipulation settles every mechanism; preserve separate design scopes.
An explicitly forced two-component solution in Experiment1 cannot be used as universal refutation of alternative dimensionality. Compare item sets,aggregation and extraction decisions.

deferred.reason: Outcome is an adapted human-actor impression scale. Preserve that result; consult original definitions and compare existing motive/character constructs before introducing a broad trait as another AI behavior. No real prosocial act or cruelty transfer measured.

deferred.term: Suppression / inconsistent mediation as a behavior
deferred.reason: A regression relationship and statistical model feature,not by itself a new psychological behavior. Retain model interpretation with existing attribution records.

deferred.term: Robot dehumanization / uncanny valley of mind / dual-process coping
deferred.reason: Proposed explanations here,not separately measured or experimentally isolated. Avoid duplicate labels or upgrading speculative mechanisms into observed AI behavior.

limitations: No new records, unread-original credit, invented annual counts or automatic principle/harm links. Existing entries gain grounded evidence and explicit contrary/null/path distinctions. Public participant datasets not downloaded; no research code executed.
